## `lv()` — Variable Summary

`lv()` provides a quick overview of variables in a data frame (or Seurat object).
It invisibly returns the original data. In a knitted document, use
`results = "asis"` so the native report tables render directly.

```{r lv-basic, results='asis', message=FALSE}
library(UtilsR)

# All variables
lv(iris)
```

```{r lv-select, results='asis', message=FALSE}
# Select specific variables
lv(iris, Species, Sepal.Length)
```

```{r lv-pattern, results='asis', message=FALSE}
# Regex pattern matching
lv(iris, pattern = "Sepal")
```

```{r lv-group, results='asis', message=FALSE}
# Grouped summary
lv(iris, Sepal.Length, group = "Species")
```

## `na()` — Missing Value Analysis

```{r na}
# Create data with NAs
df <- data.frame(
  x = c(1, NA, 3, NA, 5),
  y = c("a", "b", NA, "d", "e"),
  z = 1:5
)
check_na(df)
```

---

## `check_system()` — System Diagnostics

```{r check-system, eval=FALSE}
check_system()
```

Reports OS, R version, memory, CPU info, and loaded packages.

## `check_size()` — Object Memory Profiling

```{r check-size, eval=FALSE}
check_size()
```

Shows memory usage of all objects in the global environment, even when called
inside a function. Pass `envir = environment()` to inspect the calling
function's objects instead, and `method = "lobstr"` for a total that counts
storage shared between objects once.
